scope: Research only: building model resolution and mod-defined placement templates. No production implementation, game/mod writes, executable patching or live Nudge experiment.
address_convention: Preferred virtual addresses; function names are analyst descriptions, not recovered symbols.

chain: DDS textures, optional .gfx overrides and .anim/state/locator data

observed_entity_names.multiple_mesh_variants: building_<identifier>_1 through _N when template mesh count exceeds one

examples.note: Shared spawn-point preview entity is distinct from the naval_base building's numbered entity variants.

binary_evidence.observation: Enumerates templates, builds building_ names with optional numbered suffix, and resolves entity pointers through 0x142293530. Also resolves destroyed names and a separate special-category entity list.
Special-category path obtains name via 0x140689620, appends _entity, then uses the same entity lookup.
Instance creation selects an entity pointer from ordinary, destroyed or special cached lists. Reports invalid spawn point / missing mesh / missing entity.
Ordinary generation checks the resolved entity list before continuing; absent model definitions can prevent placement generation.

model_resolution.interpretation: The inspected Nudge/map-building path resolves named engine entities and uses cached entity pointers. It is not simply opening a .mesh file afresh for every placement. Exact asset-manager preload timing was not traced.

mesh_probe.method: Independent read-only Python probe of @@b@ header, depth-marked objects, typed integer/float/string properties; complete byte traversal of each file. No Blender or game process needed.
mesh_probe.limit: Structural decoding does not establish correct rendering, skinning, valid triangle indices for every file, or support for all DLC/custom assets. No visual render was performed.

pipeline: Load common/buildings building and explicit spawn_points definitions from the effective game/mod file set.
Synthesize templates from building display/scope fields and resolve explicit spawn_point indirection.
Enumerate resolved, unredirected templates in Nudge; separately append the built-in floating-harbor category.
Resolve preview entities and calculate required graphical placement counts for the selected state.
Run the shared land/centered/coastal generator, or built-in special generator, then serialize graphical placement records.
data_driven_controls: show_on_map controls graphical placement count; it is distinct from level_cap construction limits.
province_max presence/positive scope data distinguishes provincial buildings from state buildings; explicit templates use type = state or province.
Explicit spawn_points use max; multiple buildings can share one named spawn point.
only_costal is the actual misspelled key; it selects coastal eligibility, not the floating-harbor algorithm.
centered is parsed by the spawn-point parser and copied from generated building templates.
disable_auto_nudging excludes the template from automatic reconciliation; vanilla dams, locks and landmarks use it.
show_on_map_meshes controls entity variants, not the number of independent placement rows.
practical_custom_workflow: Define the custom building in common/buildings and choose its graphical scope/count, or reference an explicitly named spawn point.
Provide matching building_<identifier> entity definitions and their pdxmesh/mesh/texture dependencies; shared spawn points need their own preview entity, as vanilla naval_base_spawn demonstrates.
Load the mod in the game and use Nudge's selected-state placement/reconciliation workflow. This workflow is inferred from the inspected common pipeline, not a newly executed custom-mod experiment.
Store resulting coordinates in map/buildings.txt. These graphical locations do not themselves set constructed building levels in state history or create gameplay effects.
record_notes: The first field is a state ID, not a province ID.
The name can be a shared spawn-point name rather than the gameplay building name.
Ordinary port links identify a sea province; floating-harbor links identify the associated land province. Preserve these distinct semantics.

binary_evidence.observation: Builds the spawn-point database and resolves named/shared points. Error string explicitly rejects a building and named spawn point having the same identifier.
Synthesizes template fields from a building, including scope, count, mesh count and flags.
Spawn-point parser accepts a fixed set of fields. The type branch recognizes only state and province; other values report Unknown spawn point type.
Enumerates the database's unredirected templates and appends category 1 explicitly.
Reconciles a state's expected and existing placements, skipping auto-nudging-disabled templates and generating deficits. Removal branches also exist.

token_crosscheck.method: Cross-reference token-registration strings and their constant IDs against parser comparisons, not string naming alone.

floating_harbor.classification: Built-in category 1, not an ordinary mod-declared spawn-point type.
floating_harbor.name_mapping: 0x140689620 recognizes category 1; its string descriptor at 0x1427e4870 points to floating_harbor.
floating_harbor.algorithm: Uses a coastal adjacency anchor and land center to offset into the selected sea, with a sea-center fallback and separate orientation logic. See coastal_placement_followup.json for prior evidence and incomplete parity results.
floating_harbor.configurable_parameter: NGraphics.DEFAULT_NUDGE_FLOATING_HARBOR_DIST = 7.0 in common/defines/00_graphics.lua:1310. This is a global parameter of the existing built-in algorithm, not a per-custom-building callback.

special_rules.conclusion: Ordinary custom buildings can reuse supported placement parameters. No user-defined placement algorithm hook was found in the inspected parser, template enumeration or generator dispatch. Giving a custom building a new name, coastal flag, or floating-harbor-looking model does not by itself route it into the built-in special category.
special_rules.manual_layouts: For irregular landmarks/bridges/dams or a scripted composition, authored coordinates and auto-nudging exclusion are the evidenced vanilla pattern. An editor-side custom placement rule could generate supported records, but would not extend the game's accepted record types or runtime behavior.
special_rules.not_claimed: This is a bounded static-analysis conclusion, not a proof that no other engine subsystem offers any workaround. It does not establish the validity of arbitrary offshore ordinary-building coordinates.

future_editor_design: Resolve effective game/mod assets, including path replacement and duplicate-name precedence, before building entity and mesh indexes; exact collision precedence still requires testing.
Keep gameplay building identity, resolved graphical spawn-point identity, entity identity, and built-in special category separate.
Preserve repeated blocks in .asset/.gfx parsing; a dictionary parser that overwrites repeated entity/pdxmesh/meshsettings keys is insufficient.
Read geometry, material references and overrides, entity scale and coordinate conventions before adding animations/particles/shader parity.
Actual model geometry can be used with an orthographic map or separate selected-model preview; restoring tilted-map interaction is not a requirement.
If unknown custom placement constraints are encountered, preserve existing records and expose unsupported rules rather than silently using ordinary random placement.
remaining_validation: Live Nudge experiment with one custom state building, one provincial building, one shared spawn point, and missing-entity negative case.
Provincial max > 1: prior static expected-count routine does not simply multiply province count by max; keep this unresolved until live testing.
Exact mesh-variant selection, asset overrides/copy_from and mod/DLC load precedence.
DDS decoding and visual comparison of material overrides, handedness, UV orientation, entity scale, skinning and animations.
Floating-harbor parity remains partial: the previous shipped-record comparison was not a fresh live Nudge run.
